newsitem.title: DUBAI: Canadian navy stops ship over U.N. Iraq sanctions.
newsitem.headline: Canadian navy stops ship over U.N. Iraq sanctions.

text.p: A Canadian frigate detained a merchant ship in the Gulf on suspicion of breaking United Nations sanctions against Iraq, the Canadian navy reported late on Monday.
It said in a statement sent to Reuters the frigate Regina intercepted Qabas 2, an offshore replenishment vessel which was sailing from Iraqi waters into international waters in the Gulf on May 3.
"All of the evidence found on the merchant ship led officials to believe that the Qabas 2 was in violation of U.N. trade embargo sanctions," it said.
A second vessel suspected of breaking sanctions was also intercepted by the Regina and diverted to a holding area for further investigation.
The Canadian frigate is part of a multinational force that checks shipping in the Gulf to enforce U.N. sanctions against Iraq imposed afer its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Since 1990 vessels from 14 countries have contributed ships to the force, which has intercepted more than 22,000 merchant ships and diverted more than 500 for carrying contraband cargo or inaccurate documents.
